title: 12V Battery Check & Replacement
subtitle: Slow cranks and random electronics glitches often start at the 12V battery — we'll test, clean, and replace safely.
tone: Encouraging coach with strong electrical safety. Hybrids/EVs still have a 12V battery — call that out early. Prefer short steps + GIFs for clamp order.
prerequisites: Correct group size / cold cranking amps (CCA) for your vehicle
Memory saver optional (radio/windows may need relearn)
For AGM vs flooded: match what the car was designed for
tools_checklist: Terminal brush / baking soda + water for corrosion

adaptive_rules.coach_note: Many 12V batteries fade between years 3–5 (heat kills them faster in hot climates). Test before a cold snap.
Start-stop systems usually need AGM (or the OEM-specified type). Putting a cheap flooded battery in an AGM car shortens life and can set charging faults.
Hybrids and EVs still rely on a 12V battery for computers and contactors. A 'dead EV' is often a 12V issue — but high-voltage orange cables are off-limits.
Many European cars need battery registration / coding after replacement. DIY swap is possible, but a shop with a scan tool prevents charging errors.
Trucks with winches, plows, or dual batteries need the right CCA and sometimes a matched pair — don't mix old/new randomly.

steps.title: Let's check the 12V heartbeat
steps.description: Slow crank, clicking starter, flickering lights, or a car that 'randomly dies' — we'll measure the 12V battery first. No shame if it's due; heat and short trips are hard on them.
steps.safety_warning: Batteries can explode from sparks near charging/gassing. Eye protection on. Never lean over while clamping.

action_buttons.label: Won't start / jump needed
action_buttons.payload: My car needs a jump or won't start. Coach me on safe jump-pack use for my vehicle.

variants.title: 12V still matters on hybrids/EVs
variants.description: We'll stay on the small 12V battery only. Orange high-voltage cables and under-hood junction boxes are off-limits.
variants.safety_warning: Do not cut, unbolt, or probe orange HV cables. If the 12V is buried or in the trunk with HV nearby, prefer a shop.

steps.title: Resting & charging voltage
steps.description: Engine off ~12.4–12.7V is healthy for a rested flooded/AGM. Below ~12.1V is discharged. Running often ~13.7–14.7V if the alternator/DC-DC is charging. Pair with a load test when you can.
steps.safety_warning: Don't short the probes across posts. Keep jewelry away from terminals.

steps.title: Clean corrosion (quick DIY win)
steps.description: If posts are fuzzy white/green, clean with a terminal brush (baking soda mix for flooded corrosion). Tight, clean clamps fix many 'dead battery' ghosts.
steps.safety_warning: Disconnect negative first if you remove clamps to clean. Neutralize acid residue; wash skin if splashed.

steps.title: DIY swap or let a shop code it?
steps.description: Many gas cars are a straightforward DIY. AGM start-stop, trunk batteries, IBS sensors, or European registration push this toward a parts-store install or indie shop — still a smart call.
steps.safety_warning: Wrong battery type (AGM vs flooded) or skipping registration can cause charging faults.

variants.description: Plan on battery registration with a scan tool after the swap. If you don't have one, buy the battery and pay for install/coding.
If access is tight near HV components, choose a shop. Your job is the 12V only.

steps.title: Remove old, install new (clamp order)
steps.description: Negative (−) off first, then positive (+). Swap the battery, secure the hold-down, connect positive first, negative last. Coat terminals lightly. Confirm no tools left on the posts.
steps.safety_warning: Sparks near a gassing battery are dangerous — negative first off / last on reduces short risk if a wrench hits ground.

action_buttons.label: Hold-down / tray rusted
action_buttons.payload: Battery hold-down or tray is rusted/seized. How do I proceed safely?

steps.title: Start, verify, relearn windows/radio
steps.description: Start the car, recheck charging voltage, clear any obvious warnings. You may need window 'up + hold' relearns, clock/radio codes, or a scan tool for battery registration.
steps.safety_warning: If you smell sulfur, see smoke, or cables heat up, shut down and disconnect carefully — get help.

action_buttons.label: Warning lights remain
action_buttons.payload: After battery replacement I still have warning lights. Help me sort registration vs other faults.

steps.title: Log the battery birthday
steps.description: Save install date, brand, and group size in your health file. Recycle the old battery (most parts stores credit the core). Nice work keeping roadside drama away.

completion.title: 12V service done — systems online
completion.description: Expect 3–5+ years from a quality AGM in moderate climates. Retest before winter if you take lots of short trips.
